 3 UK Dividend Stocks Built For Sticky Inflation
 Bailey Pemberton Wed, November 11, 2026 at 8:11 PM EST 5 min read CWK.L +0.18% 
 ABF.L +0.63% 
 HFG.L +0.41% 
 Persistent UK inflation above the 2% target and the prospect of higher-for-longer interest rates have turned the hunt for resilient dividend payers into more than a side quest. Cash in the bank may lag rising prices, while some equities could see valuations pressured. This article focuses on three UK stocks exposed to that inflation story, all drawn from a dividend and value screener designed for tougher conditions. 
 The three stocks below are only a sample of what fits this inflation-resilient, dividend and value theme, and the full screen surfaced 8 more large UK companies with similarly robust stories that are not covered here. If you want to identify candidates that better match your own risk tolerance and income goals, head straight into the UK Inflation-Resilient Dividend and Value Stocks screener to filter and analyze the wider list. 
 Cranswick (LSE:CWK) 
 Overview: Cranswick is a UK-based food producer supplying pork, poultry and other chilled foods to supermarkets and food service customers, offering inflation-resilient consumer staples. 
 Operations: Cranswick generates about £3.0b of annual revenue, with roughly £2.9b from food products and the vast majority earned in the United Kingdom. 
 Market Cap: £2.9b 
 Cranswick fits this screener because it sells everyday food products, has a long record of paying dividends and operates in a defensive consumer category where pricing power and cost pass through really matter, according to DKDGI, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote a detailed thesis on the business. 
 "Risks: heavy investment years push the payout to 60 to 70% of free cash flow after leases; animal disease; dependence on major UK grocers." 
 What happens to that carefully balanced income profile if one unseen pressure on its cash generation starts to bite harder? 
 If that cash squeeze worry is front of mind, read the full narrative for Cranswick to see how Cranswick's investment cycle, payouts and risks all fit together. 
 LSE:CWK Revenue & Expenses Breakdown as at Nov 2026 Hilton Food Group (LSE:HFG) 
 Overview: Hilton Food Group is a multi-protein food supplier packing meat, seafood, plant-based products and ready meals for major international supermarkets. 
 Operations: Hilton Food Group reports around £4.5b in segment-adjusted revenue, primarily from its multi-protein supply agreements and related services. 
 Market Cap: £667 million 
 Hilton Food Group slots into this inflation-resilient dividend and value theme because it is tied to everyday grocery spending, and the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St points to a business shaped by long-term supply deals with powerful retailers rather than short-term volume swings. 
 Story Continues "Strategic partnerships and long-term supply contracts with leading retailers (Tesco, Walmart, Ahold Delhaize) are providing resilience and revenue stability, offering a buffer against short-term market volatility and ensuring steady cash generation for reinvestment and dividends." 
 The real test for Hilton Food Group is how one unresolved pressure on its thin margins and funding costs ultimately plays out. 
 If that margin squeeze is what you are watching, go straight to the full narrative for Hilton Food Group to see how Hilton Food Group's contracts, capex and capital structure could be decoupling. 
 LSE:HFG Revenue & Expenses Breakdown as at Nov 2026 Associated British Foods (LSE:ABF) 
 Overview: Associated British Foods runs the Primark retail chain and a broad food and ingredients portfolio, anchoring it firmly in everyday consumer staples. 
 Operations: Associated British Foods generates most of its £21.5b revenue from Primark retail at about £9.8b, alongside sizeable grocery, sugar, agriculture and ingredients divisions. 
 Market Cap: £13.9b 
 Associated British Foods fits into this inflation-resilient dividend and value theme through Primark-led retail and a wide staples footprint. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St highlights how operational tweaks, rather than big headline moves, are doing much of the defensive heavy lifting. 
 "The rollout of digital initiatives and Click & Collect in Primark has moved on, with nationwide coverage in Great Britain and strong website traffic growth." 
 The real swing factor for investors is how one less visible pressure on Associated British Foods' pricing power and profitability ultimately resolves. 
 That quiet pressure on pricing power is exactly what the full narrative for Associated British Foods unpacks, highlighting where Associated British Foods could be masking both risk and upside potential.
